newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU oilseed industry attacks farm reform plan.
newsitem.headline: EU oilseed industry attacks farm reform plan.

text.p: Proposed farm reforms to prepare for EU expansion eastwards would slash aid to oilseeds farmers and force them to switch to cereals, the EU Seed Crushers and Oil Processors' Federation said.

In Agenda 2000, the European Commission this week proposed a single area aid payment of 66 ecus a tonne for all crops, which if approved by farm ministers, would result in a sharp cut for oilseed producers currently receiving 94 ecus a tonne.
But cereals farmers, who currently get 54.35 ecus a tonne, stand to gain a 22 percent increase. Cereals, unlike oilseeds, also benefit from an intervention price safety net.
"Such a policy will have disastrous consequences for the European oilseeds processing industry," FEDIOL said in a statement, adding it was a clear signal to abandon oilseeds production.
It warned that the EU, which is only some 20 percent self-sufficient in proteins and 45 percent in vegetable oils, would become even more dependent on imports.

Oilseed crushers and processors will find it increasingly difficult to remain a stable supplier of proteins, vegetable oils and fats to consumers at competitive prices, it said, noting surging world raw materials demand, notably in Asia.
It complained that some oilseed producing countries were protecting their industries whereas the EU had opened its borders for oilseed and protein trade.
"EU industry must have access on equal terms to raw materials from producing nations as well as finished product markets and not only be the dumping ground of processed products," it said.
"The proposed changes in the CAP-2000 only reinforce this position and will lead to a substantial destruction of oilseed processing capacity if maintained," it warned.
EU farm ministers will give their initial reactions to the reform proposals at a meeting in Brussels on Tuesday.
